oneliner.t: Former FBI agent, state senator and seven-term U.S. House member who chaired the House Intelligence Committee (2011–2015), lost the 2024 Senate race to Elissa Slotkin by about 19,000 votes, and is the Trump-endorsed, unopposed Republican nominee for Michigan's open Senate seat in 2026.

hometown.t: Brighton Township, Livingston County, Michigan (Howell High School, 1981)

upbringing.t: Born in Livonia to Joyce A. and John C. Rogers. He spent his early years in Redford Township before the family moved to Brighton Township in Livingston County. He graduated from Howell High School in 1981 and from Adrian College in 1985 with a degree in criminal justice and sociology. He served in the U.S. Army (1985–1989), then was an FBI special agent in Chicago (1989–1994), working organized crime and public corruption. His brother Bill Rogers later served as a state representative.

career.role: Special agent (Chicago office; organized crime, public corruption)
U.S. Representative, MI-8; Chair, House Intelligence Committee 2011–2015
Board member, then chair of the board of trustees (elected 2021)

platform.t: Bring manufacturing jobs back, cut taxes for working families, put shop classes in every high school, and lower costs. He blames Democratic policies and state energy standards for an 'artificial increase' in energy prices.
Allow tax-free 529 withdrawals for first-time homebuyer down payments, roll back housing regulations, and add incentives for builders (plan announced Feb. 2026).

Opposes 'free health care for all' and opposed extending enhanced ACA subsidies. Proposes expanding TrumpRx for drug prices and penalizing providers and insurers that don't post itemized prices or that deny care excessively.
Local control. Communities should not bear higher energy costs, and data-center tax revenue should offset local property taxes. In Aug. 2026 he backed a one-year moratorium on new data centers.
School choice, more parental involvement, and third-grade reading assessments; 'refocus schools on education'.
Counter cyber threats from Russia, China and Iran. Supported the 2025 and 2026 strikes on Iran but says the war should end soon and that Trump should seek congressional authorization for more action.
Supports Israel as the region's only democratically elected ally.
Defends Trump's immigration strategy. At the Oct. 8 debate he said ICE's efforts in Minnesota were 'probably not appropriate'.
His Oct. 2026 ad says Canada 'is not our enemy' and calls for ending the tariff war. Earlier (Aug. 2026) he said he did not know how he would vote on Senate measures condemning Trump's tariffs.
Says he will protect Social Security.

End the tariff war with Canada.

note.t: Per PolitiFact's review of his 2025 Senate candidate report, he and his wife reported $6.7M–$13.5M in assets and no debt. Counting homes in Michigan, Virginia and Florida, PolitiFact estimated net worth at $10.1M–$16.9M, up from $415,600–$605,600 in non-property assets when he left office in 2015. His Dec. 2023 report showed about $1.975M in board and consulting payments since Jan. 2022: IronNet $724,887, Nokia $460,000, MITRE $191,000, D-Wave about $160,000, Telefónica Ingeniería over $20,000. He also got $30,000 from lobbying firm CGCN Group (his campaign says it was strategic-communications work). Forgepoint cyber funds were valued at $150K–$350K (2025). PolitiFact found no record that he ever registered as a lobbyist or worked for drug companies. His wife's board roles (NowSecure, Qualys, Forgepoint council) are her own record.

He bought a Cape Coral, Fla., home in 2022 and an exurban Detroit house in July 2023 before his 2024 run, and his registered residence was questioned in 2024 coverage.

checks.legal: Courts: CourtListener direct search was blocked for this tool (provenance), and Justia/PACER were not run. No court news search was run for him specifically, and no case surfaced in the coverage read. Ethics: House Ethics/OCE pages could not be fetched, and no ethics finding surfaced in coverage. The June 22, 2026 cease-and-desist letter his campaign sent El-Sayed is not litigation. The debate claims he made about El-Sayed's mother concern El-Sayed's relative and are not part of either candidate's legal record.
checks.foreign: FARA bulk files searched 2026-10-13: the matches are other people and firms (Edward M. Rogers Jr./BGR, George M. Rogers Jr., Rogers & Cowan, Rogers & Wells). No match for Mike or Michael Rogers. Disclosures (via PolitiFact/Business Insider/Metro Times reporting; the Senate eFD itself was not opened) show payments from foreign companies: Nokia (Finland) $460,000 and Telefónica Ingeniería (Spain) over $20,000, and Wikipedia lists a Telefónica advisory-committee seat. A 2024 Heartland Signal headline about 'connections to Saudi companies' was not opened or verified.

corp.t: Career corporate-PAC money of about $3.48M and trade-association PAC money of about $1.68M (FEC committee records, 2000–2026), plus $5.55M from lobbyist/registrant-connected PACs. In 2026 so far: corporate PACs $220,000, trade PACs $121,500. Long-running givers include UPS PAC ($79,000), Koch Inc. PAC ($64,500), the home builders' BUILD PAC ($75,000) and ABC PAC ($72,500). Pharma-linked PACs gave tens of thousands per cycle 2004–2014 (PolitiFact). Americans for Prosperity Action spent $14.2M supporting him in 2026; its funders were not checked.

lobby.t: NORPAC (pro-Israel) gave $19,590 in 2026, and Friends of Israel PAC gave $4,000 (2004–2012). Smaller country-organized PACs: ARMENPAC $2,500 (2000–2004), Armenian American Public Affairs Committee $100 (2006), and the Iranian American PAC (PAAIA) $2,500 (2012). Separately, RJC-PAC (Republican Jewish Coalition) gave $33,453 (2024–2026). He attended AIPAC-hosted fundraisers in Aug. 2026. No UDP independent expenditures for him.

research_notes: NOMINATION CONFIRMED: unopposed in the Aug. 4, 2026 GOP primary (883,328 votes) after Bernadette Smith was disqualified for insufficient signatures. Trump endorsed him (Truth Social, Aug. 5, 2026, in a post with false claims about Wayne County ballots, per WPBN, and again before the Oct. 8 debate). VOTES: 'na' because he was out of Congress during the 118th–119th key-vote window. His 2001–2014 House votes beyond the 2005 certification roll call were not compiled (Wikipedia notes the 2013 20-week abortion ban vote and repeated votes against Medicare drug-price negotiation). MONEY: FEC totals through July 15 (Q3 due Oct. 15). Itemized individual donors, industries, quarters and in-state % were not available (fec.gov/OpenSecrets blocked). AIPAC PAC earmarks were not itemized. The New Republic (Aug. 24) relays NYT reporting that AIPAC planned a multimillion-dollar ad effort for him and that he asked UDP to reconsider. No such UDP spending appears in FEC data through Oct. 13. Super PAC funders (AFP Action, GLCF, Sentinel, America PAC) were not retrieved. HOUSE DISCLOSURES: the on-disk PDFs (2008–2015) are image scans. The 2015 termination report was OCR'd only partially (Sullivan Bruyette portfolio statement for 'Michael and Kristi Rogers'), and the OCR also picked up pages that appear to belong to another filer, so no figures were taken from it. Current wealth figures come from PolitiFact/Business Insider/Metro Times reporting on his Senate filings. The Senate eFD was not opened directly. OUTSIDE THE CLAIMS SAMPLE (recorded for balance, not rated): at the Oct. 8 debate he said El-Sayed 'can't condemn Hamas' and linked him to the Muslim Brotherhood. TheGrio reports El-Sayed has explicitly condemned Hamas and that fact-checkers debunked the Brotherhood link (Bridge found no evidence). He also said El-Sayed's mother worked for a group 'indicted for funneling money' to al-Qaeda. Per TheGrio/Snopes she was never charged, and her record is not the candidate's. FAMILY: wife Kristi Rogers' board and advisory roles are her own record. RESIDENCY: Florida home (2022) and 2024 questions about his registered Michigan address (Bridge, Detroit Free Press via Wikipedia). NOT FOUND/NOT DONE: courts, ethics, FEC RFAI, Senate eFD direct read, campaign site, town halls, photo, Heartland Signal Saudi claim.
